causes: Overset text — check for a red '+' in the frame's bottom-right corner
The frame is too small for its content
Text color matches the background
The layer containing the text is hidden
fix: Check the frame corner for a red '+'; if present, resize the frame or thread it into a new one. Otherwise check text color and the Layers panel for visibility.

problem: My image looks blurry on screen and in export.
causes: Low actual resolution of the source file
Image scaled up too much inside its frame (low effective PPI)
Display Performance set to 'Fast' (screen-only, doesn't reflect final quality)
fix: Check the Links panel for Effective PPI — aim for 300 for print. If it's low, use a higher-res source or reduce the frame's scale. Also check View > Display Performance > High Quality Display.

problem: My PDF has white edges after printing.
causes: No bleed set in Document Setup
Background elements not extended into the bleed area
Bleed not included in the PDF export settings
fix: Set bleed to at least 3mm/0.125in, extend all background elements fully into it, and enable 'Marks and Bleeds' in the export dialog with bleed values matching the document.

causes: Numbers were typed manually instead of using the automatic marker
The parent page wasn't applied to all pages
A section restart was set unintentionally in Numbering & Section Options
fix: Replace manual numbers with Type > Insert Special Character > Markers > Current Page Number, confirm parent application in the Pages panel, and check Layout > Numbering & Section Options for unwanted restarts.

problem: My text box shows a red plus sign.
causes: The frame contains more text than it can display (overset)
fix: Click the red '+' out-port and thread the overflow into a new or existing frame, or enlarge the current frame, or edit the copy to fit.

problem: Fonts changed when I opened the file on another computer.
causes: The required fonts aren't installed on that computer
InDesign substituted a similar font automatically
fix: Use File > Package to bundle fonts with your project, or ensure required fonts are installed/activated (e.g. via Adobe Fonts) on any computer opening the file.

problem: My exported PDF looks different from what I see in InDesign.
causes: Wrong export preset used (e.g. Web instead of Print)
Transparency flattening changed appearance
Missing bleed/marks settings
fix: Re-export using the correct preset for your output (Print vs. Interactive), check transparency-heavy objects in Separations Preview, and confirm marks/bleed settings match your intent.

problem: My colors look different once printed.
causes: Document was designed in RGB instead of CMYK
Screen isn't color-calibrated
Printer uses a different color profile than expected
fix: Set the document's color intent to Print/CMYK from the start, use swatches instead of eyeballing colors, and check Separations Preview before sending to print.

problem: I can't click on an object — it seems stuck.
causes: The object is locked (Object > Lock)
The object is on a locked or hidden layer
Another object is stacked directly on top of it
fix: Try Object > Unlock All on Spread, check the Layers panel for locked/hidden layers, or right-click and use 'Select Next Object Below' to reach a stacked object.

problem: My paragraph style updates aren't applying to some text.
causes: That text has local overrides layered on top of the style
The text is actually using a different, similarly-named style
The text isn't actually using a paragraph style at all
fix: Check for a '+' next to the style name in the panel (indicates overrides) and use Clear Overrides (Alt/Option-click the style), and confirm the correct style is actually applied via the Paragraph Styles panel highlight.

problem: My table looks broken after pasting spreadsheet data.
causes: Data was pasted as plain text instead of using 'Insert Table' formatting
Inconsistent column counts in the source data
Existing table styles conflicting with pasted formatting
fix: Use Edit > Paste Special or the paste options dialog to explicitly convert tab-delimited data into a table, and verify column counts match before pasting.

problem: Data Merge isn't pulling in the right information.
causes: CSV column headers don't match expected field names
Wrong data source file selected/outdated
Text frame too small, causing merged text to overset silently
fix: Double-check CSV headers match your inserted fields exactly, reselect the correct data source, and enable Auto-Size on merge text frames to handle variable content length.
